headline: UC Berkeley researchers used AI to read about 7 million pages of local laws and build a free database of millions of city and county rules.
score_reason: The database has been online since June and the paper was accepted last week, so today's announcement is older news.
importance_line: Residents, journalists, city planners and researchers could compare local rules on topics like housing and building far more easily, and free tools could be built on top, but the first and largest claims are the team's own and the release does not say how accurate the AI labelling is.
summary: UC Berkeley says its researchers used an AI tool that reads scanned pages (LightOnOCR) and OpenAI models to turn nearly 10,000 hard-to-read documents, about 7 million pages, into a free, searchable database of millions of ordinances from all 50 states, which it calls the first of its kind for local laws. The team put a version online in June, and a paper about it was accepted at the NeurIPS AI conference, to be presented in December.
freshness: FOLLOW-UP of Jun 2026 (exact date not stated)
notes: Official university release. Database online since June 2026; paper accepted last week. Score lowered 4 to 3 (older event). First-of-its-kind and scale claims are the team's own.
